reviewStrategy.description: Group fresh gauges by river family, prioritize gauges on named public paddling corridors and larger drainage networks, reuse same-river source findings, and record durable per-gauge outcomes only after corridor and duplicate checks. A gauge name or drainage size alone never qualifies or disqualifies a route.

completedWindows.outcome: Published Buchanan-to-Arcadia on USGS 02019500, promoted Remington-to-Kelly's Ford as the next ready candidate on USGS 01664000, and preserved the Luray gauge family as explicit follow-on research because the screened Bixler-to-Bentonville reach uses downstream USGS 01631000.

Published Rector Tract-to-Kelly's Ford on direct USGS 01664000 after clearing current public access, WMA permit, private-bank, Class II+ safety, camping, coordinate, geometry, image, verification, test, build, and rollback gates.

Published Newport-to-White House Landing on direct USGS 01629500 after finding an exact DWR public endpoint pair within American Whitewater's encompassing Newport-to-Luray subreach. The route cleared source-backed thresholds, access rules, private-bank and Foltz Mill safety, camping, coordinate, geometry, image, independent verification, all tests, build, and rollback gates.

Screened three Shenandoah gauges separately and published the strongest survivor: a scored Meems Bottom-to-Chapman's Landing route on direct USGS 01632000. Final geometry reconciliation uses about 20.4 mapped river miles between the authoritative DWR endpoints; American Whitewater's 15-mile VA 730-to-VA 672 inventory geometry ends upstream of the current DWR ramp. USGS 01631000 remains a direct South Fork candidate pending exact public subroute distance and threshold applicability. USGS 01628500 remains blocked pending an exact direct-threshold corridor.

Closed both remaining North Fork mainstem gauges without adding a speculative route. USGS 01633000 is an existing-route gap inside the already scored Meems Bottom-to-Chapman's corridor; its source-backed guidance belongs to USGS 01632000. USGS 01634000 remains a route-capable candidate because public accesses and a named long reach exist, but no numeric runnable guidance tied to 01634000 was found and two dam/portage packages remain unresolved.

Published the exact 2.5-mile Iron Gate/Lick Run-to-Glen Wilton corridor on direct USGS 02016500 after clearing official public endpoints, American Whitewater's 400-20,000 cfs outer limits, conservative scoring, access-road and private-bank safety, camping, coordinate, geometry, image, verification, test, build, and rollback gates. Screened out stage-only USGS 02024750 at Bedford Dam because no lawful corridor/portage/threshold package exists. Preserved USGS 02024752 as a blocked route-capable candidate pending an exact below-dam public corridor, direct numeric guidance, and complete dam/access safety.

Published the exact 9.3-mile Bent Creek-to-James River State Park corridor on direct USGS 02026000 after clearing current public endpoints, American Whitewater's 800-6,000 cfs correlation, conservative scoring, park/access safety, endpoint camping, coordinates, geometry, image rights, verification, tests, build, and rollback gates. Preserved USGS 02025500 as blocked because the old 29-mile Snowdon-to-Six Mile reach lacks a current authoritative Six Mile takeout and complete long-route logistics. Preserved USGS 02029000 as blocked because the public Howardsville-to-Scottsville opportunity still lacks a numeric paddling band tied to that station.

Durably blocked all three documented paddling candidates without publishing a weak-access route. Upper Tye has a direct 250-10,000 cfs correlation but relies on Evergreen Church property for its standard put-in; Big Piney has a direct 400-2,500 cfs correlation and National Forest put-in but lacks a manager-confirmed Perkins Mill takeout and presents unresolved private-land/low-water-bridge portage hazards; Upper Rockfish has a direct 200-800 cfs correlation and plausible Wayside endpoint but lacks a current manager-confirmed Adial Bridge launch. Virginia DWR's maintained-access inventory contains none of the three rivers. Each retry condition requires materially new authoritative access evidence.

Published the exact 6.8-mile Route 6-to-Hardware River WMA bridge corridor on direct USGS 02030000 after clearing American Whitewater's 190-7,500 cfs correlation, current DWR ramp/WMA/bridge/parking evidence, mandatory bridge takeout, WMA permit and camping rules, coordinates, canonical geometry, and independent verification. Supplemental review added the exact 14-night/300-foot WMA camping limits and a rights-cleared CC BY-SA 4.0 Hardware River aqueduct image. Slate remains blocked because its only DWR result is a separate watershed/lake facility and no exact river corridor or station-specific numeric guidance was found. Mechums remains blocked because seasonal paddling context does not establish an exact public endpoint pair, DWR access, or numeric guidance tied to 02031000.

Closed the Rivanna headwaters window without forcing a route. Moormans remains route-capable but blocked because the standard Sugar Hollow put-in conflicts with the current no-boating rule and lower variants lack confirmed public endpoints, lawful portages, and an exact numeric package. South Fork Rivanna is screened out because official use is reservoir paddling rather than a gauge-responsive point-to-point route; below-dam mainstem routes require their own gauge relationship. North Fork Rivanna remains route-capable but blocked because neither endpoint is confirmed public, two dam portages are unresolved, the source conflicts on reach distance, and reported minimum stages differ materially.

Closed two unusually strong access-ready opportunities without weakening the numeric evidence gate. DWR's exact Crofton-to-Palmyra and Cartersville-to-West View floats have current DWR-owned concrete endpoints, but neither has numeric paddling guidance tied to its exact direct gauge and corridor; generic upstream anecdotes, historical low flows, and flood stages were not transferred. Fine Creek is screened out because a fresh small-basin gauge exists but no named paddling corridor, public endpoint pair, DWR access, or threshold evidence was found.

Published the Pony Pasture Park-to-Reedy Creek corridor on direct USGS 02037500 with American Whitewater's 3.0 ft low-runnable evidence, a conservative 4.0-7.0 ft ideal band, Richmond's current 9.0 ft expert-only ceiling, the mandatory Reedy Creek takeout, current water-quality/CSO checks, public endpoints, coordinates, geometry, independent verification, tests, build, and rollback. Supplemental review now discloses the park partner's 3.5-mile estimate alongside American Whitewater's 4.5-mile estimate, links Richmond's accessible-takeout documentation and live CSO map, and adds an exact public-domain Reedy Creek image. Tuckahoe Creek is screened out because the current county park prohibits boating and its Wilton launch is only a plan concept. Little Westham Creek is screened out because its official use is a restored campus eco-corridor rather than paddling.
